tour.title: App Entry and Startup
tour.description: The binary entry point main.rs hides the Windows console in release builds and delegates to the run function in the crate root. lib.rs declares every module and wires up Tauri, shared state and windows, so it is the map for the rest of the tour. Read it first to see how the pet, chat, settings and AI features hang together.
tour.languageLesson: Rust keeps binaries thin: main.rs calls into a library crate (lib.rs), which makes the app logic testable and reusable by examples.

tour.title: Pet Motion Core
tour.description: The fleet-snowfluff-core crate holds platform-independent pet logic with no AI dependency. motion.rs is a headless state machine for wander, follow, curious and rest, tuned by constants.rs and validated config.rs. Because it is pure, the behaviour can be tested without a window or GPU.
tour.languageLesson: Rust enums with data model state machines well: each motion state is a variant and transitions are exhaustive match arms.

tour.title: Swarm, Dock, Pause and Locale
tour.description: Building on the motion state machine, swarm.rs manages 1 to 80 pets sharing one set of motion settings, and dock.rs computes where a pet sits on a foreground window. pause.rs schedules special animations during pause mode, while locale.rs, i18n.rs and voice.rs cover language resolution, embedded dictionaries and voice clips.

tour.title: Pet Windows and Management
tour.description: The app crate turns core logic into real windows. manager.rs owns pet windows across monitors, and pet.rs drives each pet's animation state, dragging and docking using the motion core from the previous steps. tray.rs and chat_pause.rs add the tray menu and pause behaviour tied to chat state.

tour.title: Rendering with wgpu
tour.description: Each pet is drawn through wgpu. gfx.rs creates the GPU context and per-pet surfaces, animation.rs decodes embedded GIFs (see assets.rs) into clips, and pet_quad.wgsl is the shader that draws the sprite as a full-screen quad. This produces transparent, per-pixel-alpha pets.
tour.languageLesson: WGSL shaders can generate geometry from the vertex index, so no vertex buffer is needed to draw a full-screen quad.

tour.title: OS Platform Layer
tour.description: Window layering differs by operating system, so the platform module compiles one backend per target. macOS uses NSWindow levels, Windows attaches to WorkerW, and Linux uses X11 via GTK, each also detecting the foreground window that the docking logic relies on.
tour.languageLesson: Rust uses #[cfg(target_os = ...)] to conditionally compile platform modules, so only the relevant backend exists in each build.

tour.title: AI Provider Abstraction
tour.description: The fleet-snowfluff-ai crate starts with shared contracts. message.rs defines chat types, provider.rs the AiProvider trait, and tool_provider.rs an opt-in extension for tool calling. Concrete backends such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Ollama plug in behind the trait, with settings.rs describing provider profiles.
tour.languageLesson: Rust traits act as interfaces. Async streaming providers return boxed streams so different backends share one signature.

tour.title: Agent Loop and Native Tools
tour.description: agent_runtime.rs is the tool-calling loop: it streams a provider reply, runs requested tools, and feeds the results back. Tools implement the trait in agent_tool.rs and include file access, shell commands and web search. task_router.rs picks an execution route, and the app-side chat_commands.rs connects this to the chat window.

tour.title: Prompt Context and Memory
tour.description: Requests are assembled by prompt.rs and context_manager.rs within budgets from context_budget.rs. The memory subsystem stores long-term facts in SQLite (memory/store.rs), ranks them (rank.rs) and injects a digest (block.rs) into prompts. This is how the pet remembers the user across sessions.

tour.title: Conversation Compaction
tour.description: When history outgrows its budget, compaction.rs folds older turns into a rolling summary (summary.rs). scheduler.rs decides when to run it, memory/extraction.rs pulls durable facts from the folded segment, and compaction_runtime.rs runs all of it in the background after replies.

tour.title: MCP Client
tour.description: The MCP client lets the agent use external tools. protocol.rs implements JSON-RPC initialize, tools/list and tools/call over the McpTransport trait, with stdio and HTTP transports and an OAuth flow. tool.rs adapts each discovered tool to the agent Tool trait from the earlier agent step, always requiring confirmation.

tour.title: Frontend UI and Build Config
tour.description: A single TypeScript entry, ui/src/main.ts, renders every Tauri webview window (settings, chat and more), styled with Pico.css via style.css and built by Vite. tauri.conf.json and the capabilities file define bundling and window permissions, and the Cargo manifests tie the three crates together.
tour.languageLesson: Tauri capability files grant each webview only the permissions it needs, following least privilege.
